title: You Wake Up and the Ocean Is Gone

portraits.nora: Photorealistic head-and-shoulders portrait of a Latina woman about 58, sun-weathered skin, grey-streaked black hair in a thick braid, dark brown eyes, navy boat captain's jacket, strong kind face, plain soft grey background, soft window light, 85mm lens.
portraits.mia: Photorealistic head-and-shoulders portrait of a 16-year-old girl, wavy dark-brown hair, light freckles, olive skin, hazel eyes, simple sand-colored linen shirt, curious expression, plain soft grey background, soft window light, 85mm lens.

looks.nora: Nora: Latina woman about 58, sun-weathered skin, grey-streaked black braid, navy captain's jacket, same face as her reference image
looks.mia: Mia: 16-year-old girl, wavy dark-brown hair, light freckles, olive skin, sand-colored linen shirt, same face as her reference image

style: Cinematic photorealistic film still, vertical 9:16 composition with the subject centered, natural documentary color grade, epic scale, present day unless described, no text, no letters, no numbers.

scenes.image: Vertical view through an open window at sunrise where the ocean should be: a vast dark empty basin to the horizon.
lines: [relaxed, conversational] You wake up. You pull back the curtains... and there's no ocean.
sfx: Gentle ocean waves on a beach with distant seagulls
scenes.motion: Curtains drift open revealing the vast empty basin, slow push-in.

scenes.image: A red tugboat lying on its side in mud far below a marina dock.
lines: Every ocean on Earth. Gone overnight.

scenes.image: Nora at the end of a marina dock staring down in disbelief, hands on her head, below the dock only mud and stranded boats, the sea completely gone, no water anywhere.
lines: [breathless] Where is it? Where's the water?

scenes.image: A giant container ship tilting as it settles onto a dry muddy seabed, the sea completely gone, no water anywhere.
lines: [urgent] Ships collapse onto the seabed. Ports go silent.

scenes.image: Endless glittering white salt plains to the horizon.
lines: [awed] And the seafloor? It's white. Salt, tens of meters thick.

scenes.image: Thin clouds vanishing over a dry basin.
lines: Then the rain starts to fade. Because most of it came from the ocean.

scenes.image: A long line of people with jugs at a water station in the heat.
lines: [serious] And soon, the most valuable thing on Earth... is a glass of water.

scenes.image: Earth from space with its oceans turned white.
